## Summary

Eisman explains how correlated long and short AI exposures amplify leverage risk, then focuses on shrinking hyperscaler cash flow and still-open private-credit refinancing risk. He sees more differentiation among software companies, favors long-term AI infrastructure holdings, and questions SpaceX valuation and its mixed business model.

Full transcript reviewed. Empirical claims without inspected primary outcome evidence remain unresolved; guest claims are separate from Eisman attribution. Primary outcome verification is incomplete for claims marked unresolved; these are not adverse accuracy grades.

### 006. AI capital spending is compressing cash generation at Microsoft, Amazon and Meta despite strong revenue growth.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 6:35-7:33](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=85JeTkJ-fZU&t=395s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Microsoft, Amazon and Meta filings verify substantial capital expenditure and cash-flow pressure. Amazon trailing-year FCF was negative $7.604bn. Meta expense growth also contains legal and severance charges, so the numerical cash-flow pattern alone does not establish an exclusively AI cause.

Assessment test: Compare the stated proposition with Microsoft fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter earnings call; Meta second-quarter 2026 results. Preserve the metric, reporting period and conditions; agreement on direction alone does not prove a causal explanation.

Further verification: Inspect contemporaneous primary disclosures and subsequent comparable observations through the audit cutoff.

- [Microsoft fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter earnings call](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/events/fy-2026/earnings-fy-2026-q4) (2026-07-29): Azure grew 43%, revenue 18%; adjusted EPS $4.74 grew 23%, not 30%; operating cash $55.4bn less cash PP&E $35.8bn gives FCF $19.6bn. RPO $678bn; non-OpenAI RPO growth 25%.
- [Meta second-quarter 2026 results](https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2026/Meta-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results/) (2026-07-29): Revenue $60.801bn up 28%; expenses $42.026bn up 55%, including $2.40bn legal and $1.18bn severance; EPS $6.18 down 13%; FCF $784m; annual capex guide $130-145bn.
- [Amazon Q2 2026 Form 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872426000026/amzn-20260630.htm) (2026-07-30): Trailing-year operating cash $161.403bn less net PP&E purchases $169.007bn gives free cash flow negative $7.604bn.

## Framework and tools

- Evaluate gross leverage together with common thesis exposure on both sides of a hedge fund.
- Separate real franchises from indiscriminate sector repricing.
- A high earnings multiple makes quarterly expectation gaps difficult to trade.
- Profit growth does not eliminate capital-intensity and cash-flow risks.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Hypothetical $100m long/$100m short portfolio backed by $50m equity
- Hyperscaler free cash flow
- Forward Palantir P/E
- SpaceX annualized revenue/market-cap ratio
- Company EPS, revenues and guidance

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman hosts the episode; guest turns are inferred from introductions and conversational context.
- The Goldman/FICO pairing and automobile/carriage pairing are hypothetical illustrations, not disclosed actual fund positions.
- Amazon's June-ended cash-flow period is called its fiscal year; verify whether trailing twelve months was intended.
- SpaceX's stated $1.6tn market cap divided by $31.2bn annualized revenue is about 51.3, not 54.
